_doc: 013 slice 6 — shipped coach-view tips, keyed by sense id. One plain-language line per word: when to use it and a sample line to model. A list item's tip (spotlight_item.tip, SLP-edited) overrides these; an entity name or a sense with no entry falls back to a generic line in the coach bar.
sns_0055: more — pause mid-snack or mid-play, then model "more crackers" and wait.
sns_0056: all done — model it at the natural end of things: "all done bath", "all done book".
sns_0025: help — when they struggle with something, model "help" and wait before stepping in.
sns_0021: look — point at something interesting and model "look" while you say it.
sns_0013: want — offer a choice between two things and model "want" while they reach.
sns_0015: go — before transitions, model "go": "go outside", "go car".
sns_0026: stop — model it during rough or silly play: "stop tickles", "stop running".
sns_0027: play — invite them in: model "play" while you sit down with the toys.
sns_0028: eat — at snack time, model "eat" while you take a bite yourself.
sns_0029: drink — offer the cup, model "drink", and wait a beat before helping.
sns_0014: like — model it about things they enjoy: "like bubbles", "like this song".
sns_0074: not — model it gently when correcting: "not hot", "not now".
sns_0073: yes — ask a question you know they want, model "yes", then answer it for them.
sns_0072: no — offer something silly or wrong and model "no" with a smile.
sns_0075: please — model it on their requests, never as a demand: "more please".
sns_0587: thank you — model it when they hand you something: "thank you".
sns_0567: again — when something fun ends, pause and model "again" before repeating it.
sns_0063: different — offer the wrong thing on purpose, model "different", then swap it.
sns_0030: open — at doors, jars, and boxes: model "open" and wait before opening.
sns_0031: turn — taking turns in play: model "my turn", "your turn".
sns_0041: in — during cleanup or play: model "in" while dropping pieces in the box.
sns_0042: out — taking things out of a bag or going outside: model "out".
sns_0045: up — when they want to be picked up or climb: model "up" and wait.
sns_0046: down — getting down from a lap or slide: model "down".
sns_0043: on — shoes, lights, the TV: model "on" while you do it.
sns_0044: off — taking off shoes or turning off the light: model "off".
sns_0048: here — handing things over or calling them over: model "here".
sns_0049: there — pointing at where something goes: model "there".
sns_0005: mine — model it gently during sharing moments: "mine", then "yours".
sns_0679: yours — hand them their turn or their snack and model "yours".
sns_0003: me — model it when it's your turn or your choice: "me".
sns_0002: you — model it back at them when it's their turn: "you".
sns_0082: water — at the tap or the cup, model "water" while you pour.
sns_0083: milk — pour a little, model "milk", and wait for them to ask for more.
sns_0084: juice — offer a sip, pause, then model "juice" while they reach.
sns_0113: snack — at snack time, hold up two options and model "snack".
sns_0338: bubbles — blow one round, stop, and model "bubbles" before the next.
sns_0399: blanket — at cuddle time, model "blanket" while you pull it up.
sns_0327: outside — at the door with shoes on, model "outside" and wait.
sns_0369: book — hold up a book, model "book", and wait for them to come sit.
sns_0333: ball — roll it once, hold it, and model "ball" before the next roll.
sns_0441: dog — when the dog walks in or barks, model "dog" while you point.
sns_0442: cat — when the cat appears, model "cat" while you point.
sns_0172: hurt — model it calmly at bumps and scrapes: "hurt knee", "hurt".
sns_0159: potty — at bathroom time, model "potty" on the way in.
sns_0264: sleep — at bedtime, model "sleep" while you turn the light down.
sns_0260: hug — open your arms, model "hug", and let them come to you.
